summary.tldr: Creates Criminal Code offences for making, sharing, or advertising commercial pornographic material without confirming age and consent, and for not removing it from websites after a request.
what_it_does: Defines pornographic material as a visual representation of explicit sexual activity, or of a sexual organ or anal region shown for a sexual purpose.
Makes it an offence to make pornographic material for commercial purposes without first checking that each person shown is 18 or older and gave express consent.
Makes it an offence to distribute or advertise this material unless the maker gives written confirmation of age, express consent, and no later written withdrawal of consent.
Makes website operators remove pornographic material after a written request from the maker or a person shown, and makes knowingly failing to do so an offence.

Sets penalties of up to $500,000 or 10 years in prison, allows courts to order removal or Internet limits after conviction, and lets regulations set rules for age checks, records, and removal requests.
summary.background: The bill adds new sections 172.11 to 172.14 to the Criminal Code. It also updates seizure, forfeiture, sentencing, and compensation rules to cover this material.
